releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.12
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.12 — account rename, tab completion, skills in the shared home, inspect across worktrees

Background runs, account selection and cooldowns behave as in 0.9.11.

## What's new

**`accounts rename <old> <new>` and `accounts refresh-email`.**
- `rename` moves the account's directory, cooldowns, quota snapshot and conversation bindings to the new name. It refuses while the account is in a lease or loan, lends the shared session, or the new name is taken or invalid.
- `refresh-email [<name>...] [--json]` re-reads each account's email from its token file (offline; run `accounts quota --refresh` first to have agy renew the token) and updates the pool record. A missing token, a token without an email, or an email another account already carries is reported and the record is left alone.

**Tab completion.** `agy-crew completion bash|zsh|fish` prints a completion script. It completes commands, subcommands, flags, flag values (models, efforts, `--hosts`, `--family`), account names and job ids. `agy-crew install` sets it up for you (below).

**`install` puts the skills into the shared home.** The shared home (`~/.agy-crew/shared/home`) is the HOME that `start` and pooled runs give agy, so agy now finds the `agy-crew-*` skills there too. It is a new host, `shared` (`~/.agy-crew/shared/home/.agents/skills`), included in every default install without detection; `--hosts shared` selects it alone and `uninstall` removes it with the rest.

**`install` sets up shell completion.** The scripts go to `~/.agy-crew/completions/`. bash and zsh get one marked block in their rc file (`# >>> agy-crew completion >>>` … `# <<< agy-crew completion <<<`) that sources the script; the rest of the file is never touched and a repeat install replaces the block. fish gets `~/.config/fish/completions/agy-crew.fish`; a file you wrote yourself there is left alone and reported as a conflict. A shell is set up when its rc file exists or it is your login shell. `--no-completion` skips it, `--dry-run` writes nothing, and an rc file that cannot be written only warns. `uninstall` removes the blocks and files together with the last skill link.

## Fixes

- **`inspect` now sees jobs started in other worktrees.** Each git worktree keeps its own `.agy-crew/`, so an agent working in an auto-created worktree left its jobs where `inspect` in the main checkout could not see them. `inspect` now merges the jobs of every worktree of the repository (read-only): the Jobs page and status line mark jobs from another worktree with `[worktree-name]`, a bare `inspect` picks the newest job of any worktree, and `inspect <id>` finds it wherever it ran. `--here` restricts the view to the current worktree. A corrupt `state.json` in one worktree is skipped with a warning. `status`, `wait` and `result` still look at the current worktree only.

## Behaviour change

A default `install` now also writes to the shared home and to your shell's rc file (bash, zsh) or fish completions directory. Use `--no-completion` to skip the latter. If you ran an earlier version, remove nothing: the next `install` adds both.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Open a new shell for tab completion and restart the harness for the skills. No migration is needed.

agy's skill directory for the shared home follows its `.agents/skills` convention; check with `/skills` inside `agy-crew start`.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.11
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.11 — every `start` uses the shared home

Background runs, account selection and cooldowns behave as in 0.9.10. This release changes `agy-crew start` again: the shared home from 0.9.10 is now where every interactive session runs.

## What's new

**`start <name>` runs in the shared home too.** It used to run agy as that account in the account's own HOME, so its conversations were cut off from every other account's. Now `<name>` only chooses which account lends the credential; agy runs in `~/.agy-crew/shared/home` either way, so `/resume` and `agy --continue` see the same conversations whichever account you pick. The accounts' own HOMEs are left to background runs, which need them to keep concurrent jobs apart.

- `start <name>` checks the account as before: known, enabled, signed in, not in use. A cooldown for the model's family is printed as a note but does not refuse it.
- `start` without a name picks an idle account with quota for the family, as in 0.9.10.

## Fixes

- **A join no longer launches agy on a credential that cannot work.** The shared home holds one credential at a time, so a `start` while a shared session runs joins it. Before, a `start --model <id>` whose family had no quota on the running account joined anyway, printed a note and launched agy, which then failed on its first request. It is now refused before launching agy. `start <name>` naming a different account than the running session is refused the same way. The message gives the pids of the running sessions; exit every shared agy, then start again. `start <name>` naming the running account still joins, with a note if it is cooling.

## Behaviour change

Conversations started with `start <name>` before this release live in that account's own HOME (`~/.agy-crew/accounts/<name>/home`), and `/resume` in the shared home does not list them.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Restart the harness. No migration is needed.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.10
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.10 — a shared home for `start`

Background runs, account selection and cooldowns behave as in 0.9.9. This release changes `agy-crew start` for people who use agy by hand, and fixes one quota bug.

## What's new

**`start` without an account name runs in a shared home.** Every pool account keeps its conversations in its own HOME, so a conversation started under one account could not be resumed under another. `agy-crew start` now runs agy in `~/.agy-crew/shared/home`, a HOME that belongs to no account, so `/resume` and `agy --continue` find its conversations whichever account lends the credential.

- On start, an idle account with quota for the model family lends its credential and its Cloud Code project id: it must be enabled and signed in, with no lease, loan or hold, and no cooldown or empty quota snapshot for that family. The fullest account goes first, then the least recently used. When agy exits, the credential, which agy may have refreshed, goes back to the account. If the companion is killed, it goes back on the next pool update.
- `--model <id>` chooses the family the lender needs quota for and is passed on to agy. Without it, the family of the default model (`gemini-3.8-flash`) is used.
- A second `start` while a shared session runs joins it on the same credential; the credential goes back when the last one exits.
- When no account can lend, `start` is refused before launching agy and lists each account's state.
- The lender is held for the session (shown as `shared` in `accounts list`), so background runs stay off it.
- A quota error inside an interactive session is not recorded as a cooldown. Run `accounts quota --refresh` before starting again if the next pick might choose the same account.

`start <name>` still runs as that account in its own HOME, and now accepts `--model` too.

**Behaviour change:** a bare `start` used to print its usage and exit 1. It now starts the shared session; use `start --help` for the usage and the account list.

## Fixes

- `accounts quota --refresh` no longer stores the lender's quota under a borrower's name. While an account's credential is on loan to a running job, its token file holds the lender's credential, so the refresh now skips that account and keeps its last snapshot.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Restart the harness. No migration is needed.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.9
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.9 — `inspect`, a live tabbed viewer

Runs, account selection, cooldowns and quota behave as in 0.9.8. This release adds one command for people: `agy-crew inspect`.

## What's new

**`inspect [<job>]`** is a resident, tmux-style full-screen window for watching jobs while they run.

- Tab 0 is the **Jobs** page: recent jobs, running first, or `No tasks currently running.` when idle. Select one and press Enter to open it, including finished jobs.
- Every running job gets its own tab, including jobs started after the window opened. A tab tails the job's event stream: one line per tool call (`▶` start, `✓`/`✗` finish with duration and an output excerpt) plus the model's reply, and a status line with state, model, account, elapsed time, tool/error counts, tokens and the last tool.
- The window never exits on its own; finished jobs stay as tabs and an idle window waits for the next job. `q` or Ctrl-C quits, and quitting never cancels or signals a job.
- Keys: `Tab`/`←→` switch, `0`–`9` jump, `↑↓` `PgUp` `PgDn` `g` `End` scroll, `Enter` open, `x` close a tab, `m` toggle the mouse.
- Mouse: the wheel scrolls (or moves the selection on the Jobs page); clicking a tab switches, clicking a job row opens it. While mouse reporting is on, hold Shift to select text as usual, or start with `--no-mouse`.
- It is read-only: it does not write `state.json` and does not affect `wait`.

**`inspect <job> --plain`** is the scriptable form (also used when stdout is not a terminal, or with `--no-follow`): a scrolling log of one job that follows it to the end and exits with the job's code (0/3/4/5). `--no-color` disables colour.

A job that finished warning-free has no raw event stream left (unchanged behaviour); its tab says so and points to `result`. Agents should keep using `wait` and `observe`; `inspect` is for people.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Restart the harness. No migration is needed.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.8
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.8 — Gemini quota is back in `accounts quota`

Runs, account selection and cooldowns behave as in 0.9.7. This release fixes `accounts quota --refresh`, which had stopped reporting the Gemini pool.

## Changes since 0.9.7

**Gemini quota snapshots.** Cloud Code now returns the Gemini group from `retrieveUserQuotaSummary` only when the request's User-Agent names a recent agy CLI (`antigravity/cli/<version> (...)`, as agy itself sends). agy-crew sent a bare `antigravity`, so every refresh came back with the Claude/GPT pool only: `accounts list` and `accounts quota` showed no `gemini` rows, and `auto` could neither rank accounts by Gemini quota left nor skip an account whose Gemini quota was empty. agy's own usage view was unaffected.

Quota requests now send `antigravity/cli/<version> (aidev_client; os_type=<os>; arch=<arch>)`, with the version read from `agy --version` once per refresh (1.4.9 when it cannot be read). Run `agy-crew accounts quota --refresh` once after upgrading to bring the Gemini snapshots back.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
agy-crew accounts quota --refresh
```

Restart the harness. No migration is needed.
